client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: A mechanically ventilated adult is receiving care to reduce ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) risk. Which oral-care practice is recommended as an essential prevention strategy?

options.A: Provide daily oral care with toothbrushing without routine chlorhexidine
options.B: Use chlorhexidine with every episode of oral care as the preferred routine antiseptic
options.C: Omit toothbrushing while the client remains mechanically ventilated
options.D: Limit oral care to once weekly unless visible oral debris is present

rationale: The 2022 SHEA/IDSA/APIC practice recommendation identifies daily oral care with toothbrushing, without chlorhexidine, as an essential practice for preventing VAP/VAE in mechanically ventilated adults. Routine oral chlorhexidine is specifically not recommended because benefit is unclear and possible harm has been reported. Therefore A is the best answer. B conflicts with the current recommendation, while C and D provide less oral care than the recommended daily toothbrushing practice.
educational_objective: Provide daily toothbrushing without routine chlorhexidine as part of evidence-based oral care for mechanically ventilated adults to reduce VAP risk.
source_organization: Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA), Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA), Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology (APIC), American Hospital Association, and The Joint Commission
source_document_title: Strategies to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, ventilator-associated events, and nonventilator hospital-acquired pneumonia in acute-care hospitals: 2022 Update
source_locator: Section 4, Recommended strategies to prevent VAP/VAE in adult patients > Essential practices > 'Provide oral care with toothbrushing but without chlorhexidine': provide daily oral care with toothbrushing without chlorhexidine; 'Approaches that should not be considered a routine part' > oral care with chlorhexidine
source_claim_supported: For mechanically ventilated adults, daily oral care with toothbrushing without chlorhexidine is an essential VAP/VAE prevention practice; routine chlorhexidine oral care is not recommended.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8 / PDF p.12: protect clients and health care personnel from health and environmental hazards and infection
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — prevention of healthcare-associated respiratory infection
correction_summary: Removed the outdated universal claim that ventilated adults require basic oral care every 2–4 hours and brushing at least twice daily. Replaced it with the current SHEA/IDSA/APIC essential practice of daily toothbrushing without routine chlorhexidine. Corrected the blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control because the tested construct is VAP prevention, not hygiene comfort. Rebuilt all distractors and adjusted difficulty from hard to moderate.
audit_findings: A exactly matches the current essential-practice recommendation. B conflicts with guidance that routine oral chlorhexidine is not recommended; C and D omit or substantially underprovide the recommended daily toothbrushing. The item does not invent an every-2-to-4-hour interval, antiseptic requirement, or bundle-specific universal protocol. One clearly best answer remains with no cueing or unresolved conflict.
